title: Saskatoon police involved in second shooting in less than a week - Winnipeg Free Press
subtitle: Breaking News, Sports, Manitoba, Canada
article: This article was published 27/12/2007 (6457 days ago), so information in it may no longer be current.
SASKATOON - Criminal charges are being considered against a woman who was shot by Saskatoon police officers, Chief Clive Weighill said Friday.
The Thursday afternoon shooting, which seriously injured the woman, marked the second time in a week that city officers fired on a suspect. Last Saturday a man died from a Saskatoon police bullet.

Weighill told a news conference that in the latest incident, police received a 911 call from a distraught female just before 3 p.m. Thursday. A short time later, a caller from a neighbourhood southwest of the downtown reported seeing a woman in the street armed with knives.
"Two constables attended the scene and were immediately confronted by an agitated and aggressive female armed with a knife in each hand," he said.

"The officers attempted to defuse the situation by repeatedly directing the woman to drop the weapon. The woman continued to advance towards one of the officers, at which point the constable discharged her firearm," Weighill said.
A third officer then arrived on the scene and the woman was physically subdued to remove at least one of the knives still in her hand, Weighill said.
Still aggressive, the woman was handcuffed, he said. An ambulance was called.
The unidentified woman, 35, suffered a gunshot wound to the chest and was listed Friday in serious but stable condition in hospital.
Saskatchewan's justice minister has asked the RCMP to oversee the investigation into the latest police shooting.
"This is the second time in a week that officers have had to discharge their firearms to protect themselves or another officer," Weighhill said.
Early last Saturday, two Saskatoon police officers shot and killed Dwayne Charles Dustyhorn, 38, a man they said was threatening their colleague with two knives.

Both Dustyhorn and the woman shot Thursday are aboriginal. Weighill said he's told the Federation of Saskatchewan Indian Nations that its special investigative unit will have full access to the investigations of both incidents.
"As the chief of police, I am concerned with the risks faced by our officers on a daily basis," the chief said.
Most of these incidents can be defused without harm to the aggressor or the police, he noted.
"There are, however, unfortunate incidents such as these, where officers must make a split-second decision to protect themselves, their partner and the public," Weighill said.
